The chef cooks fresh pasta, risotto and wood-fired pizza in front of your guests. It comes to your table hot, and the price is set by your guest count, menu and service level, so the same kitchen scales from an intimate villa dinner to a 200-guest reception. MyCHEF matches you with a chef who plans the menu, cooks in front of your guests, serves and clears up. add_block.new_heading: What is on an Italian catering menu in Dubai?

Fresh-made pasta and risotto take the centre — hand-rolled tagliatelle, filled ravioli, slow-cooked ragù, saffron or wild-mushroom risotto. Wood-fired and Roman-style pizza, whole roasted fish and osso buco carry the mains, and tiramisu, panna cotta and cannoli close things out. We plan each italian menu dubai around the season, your guests and any restrictions, so vegetarian, gluten-free and halal versions are built in from the start, not bolted on at the end. Want plated courses for a formal dinner, a buffet for value, or live stations where the chef finishes pasta in front of guests? Tell us what your table loves and we shape it to match.

add_block.new_heading: The full Italian catering menu, course by course
new_paragraphs: This is the working menu bank the chefs build from, laid out in the order an Italian table runs. A buffet usually takes four to eight items per course; a plated dinner takes one or two and goes deeper on each. Nothing below is a fixed package. You mark what your table wants, the chef says what is at its peak that week, and the agreed list goes into the written quote before anything is confirmed. Ingredients are seasonal, so a tomato dish in February and the same dish in September are not identical, and the chef will say so instead of substituting quietly.

One structural note that shapes the whole menu: the Italian salumi line is rebuilt from halal beef, veal, turkey and duck instead of pork. That is not a compromise course, it is how the good kitchens here work. Beef bresaola, Salame Milano, truffle-infused beef salami, Italian veal ham, roast turkey from Italy, duck prosciutto and beef pastrami carry the charcuterie board, and the boards read as generously as any in the city.

These are what circulate while guests are still arriving, and they are the course most often under-ordered. Five to eight items is the usual spread.

Pane e focaccia: the bread course

This is bakery work, not a basket of rolls, and it is where a menu quietly proves itself. Dough is fermented for 72 hours before it is shaped, and the focaccia are named for the regions they come from. Vegetariano e contorni: vegetable mains and sides
Three to five sides plus one or two vegetable mains. These are dishes an Italian kitchen would serve anyway, not a plate assembled around an absence.
Parmigiana: layers of eggplant, mozzarella and parmesan, basil, tomato sauce

Dolci: dessert
Three to six on a buffet, eight to twelve if you take a dessert station. The tiramisù is made to a handwritten family recipe dated 1958, and it is the dish guests ask about afterwards.

Live stations: food made in front of your guests

One to three stations is the normal load for an event. Ask which tier you are buying, because two things get sold under the same name: a station where the base arrives pre-made and is finished in front of guests, and a station where the chef makes the base at your event. Those are quoted as separate lines here, since they are different amounts of work.

Pasta station : the guest picks the shape (penne, spaghetti or fusilli), the sauce and the toppings, and it is cooked to order. Sauces run pesto, Alfredo, arrabbiata, Bolognese, carbonara and piccante.
Risotto bar : a custom risotto built from a choice of sauces and toppings.

Pizza station : a pizzaiolo works a wood-fired oven on site: Margarita, The Fun Guy with truffle mushroom, Goat Cheese and Pumpkin, Tiger Jones with prawns, Italian Stallion with wagyu and peppercorn, Garden Bound with smoked chicken and asparagus, The Buffalo, and Quadrado with four cheeses. Dough is worked by hand and rested for 72 hours.
Kids pizza station : Margarita, turkey ham and pineapple, BBQ smoked chicken, plus s'more and banoffee pizzas for pudding.

Gelato cart : up to six flavours chosen from pistachio, hazelnut, Italian crema, Nutella, tiramisù, lemon and basil, dark chocolate, mango, raspberry, passion fruit and Dubai chocolate, with optional live gelato making at the cart.
Bruschetta and crostini station : cut, topped and handed over as guests come past.
Grill station : beef, chicken, lamb, fish and prawns, mushroom and cottage cheese over open heat.

Live fire is the one thing a venue can veto. Open charcoal is not permitted at many Dubai rooftops, on yachts, or in hotel function space, and gas or electric equipment is often the condition of getting in at all. That gets checked with the venue or building management before the format goes into your quote, so the answer arrives while you can still change the menu.
Grazing tables, boxes and platters

Grazing tables get booked most often for New Year's Eve, anniversaries and home brunches. They are built to a stated weight of cheese, charcuterie and fruit per person, and that weight is written into your quote, not left to the eye. Tables scale for 10, 20 or 60 guests.

The Vegan Crudités Box: seasonal crudités and baby vegetables, red pepper hummus, avocado hummus, almond-stuffed olives, crackers and breadsticks

Cheese boards with washed rind, cheddar and blue cheese, with accompaniments
Canapés and finger food
Six to ten pieces per person is the working figure for a standing reception. Canapés come by the box in 12, 24, 30 or 48 pieces, and the chef's assorted selection is the option most people take.
Sun-dried tomato, burrata and rocket

Goat's cheese, fig and truffle honey tarts

Truffle mushroom risotto pots and rose rigatoni pasta pots
Bases chosen separately: crostini, blini, tartlet, skewer, spoon, glass, thyme shortbread, vol-au-vent
Dietary variants, written down honestly
Italian is an accommodating cuisine in some directions and a stubborn one in others. Here is where each variant lands.
Halal : the salumi line is rebuilt from beef, veal, turkey and duck, so the charcuterie course stands instead of disappearing.

Vegetarian : aubergine parmigiana, sweet potato gnocchi, spinach and ricotta ravioli, trofie al pesto, caprese, vegetable lasagne, mushroom and truffle arancini, Nerano and cacio e pepe are vegetarian as written.

Vegan : a section of its own: vegan arancini alla Siciliana, pasta alla Norma, green risotto, Tuscan flatbread with spicy tomato sauce, mock-meat polpette, soy-chunk shepherd's pie, vegan chocolate mousse, and the sorbetti for dessert. Vegan recipes are not suitable for milk or egg allergies, which is a separate question.
Gluten-free : gluten-free pasta is available, and risotto and polenta are the naturally wheat-free mains. Pastry and canapé bases are the harder half; flag it while shortlisting.
Nut-free : pine-nut pesto and the pistachio dolci are the standing risk items. Both have alternatives, but they have to be chosen, not assumed.

Dairy-free : the hardest variant in this cuisine. Tomato-based pastas such as pomodoro, arrabbiata, puttanesca and Norma, olive-oil dressed antipasti, and the sorbetti are what the menu gets built from.
No alcohol in the cooking or the glass : 0% wine is used for sangria and mimosa stations, and marsala or wine-based sauces are made with a stated substitute, and the substitute is named on the menu.

The honest limit: preparation methods mean a dish cannot be described as allergen-free. Allergen requirements go to the licensed culinary partner before a booking is confirmed, and the partner assesses the ingredients, the preparation environment and the cross-contact controls, then says whether the menu can be produced as asked. If the answer is no, you hear it before you pay, not on the night.

add_block.new_heading: Italian catering delivery and drop-off in Dubai
new_paragraphs: Italian catering delivery in Dubai is a real option here, and it is priced from AED 90 per person for 10 guests or more. The food arrives ready to serve, in trays you put out yourself: antipasti and cured meats, a baked pasta that travels well, arancini, roasted vegetables, focaccia and a tiramisu tray. Nobody stays to serve it, so the saving is the staffing.

What does not travel is the part Italian cooking is built on. Fresh pasta finished in the pan, a risotto stirred to order and a pizza out of a wood-fired oven are all dishes with a two-minute window, and they are worse for the drive. If those are what you want, the chef comes to you instead and the price moves to the staffed tier. The menu we send for a drop-off is deliberately different from the plated one: it is built from dishes that are as good an hour later, not from the ones that photograph best.

add_block.new_heading: Italian restaurant or Italian catering? What the search usually means
new_paragraphs: A fair share of the searches that reach this page are for a table, not a booking: an Italian restaurant in Dubai Hills or Dubai Hills Mall, an Italian restaurant Dubai Downtown for a Friday night, a fountain view seat at Dubai Mall, fine dining at a hotel dining room, an Italian restaurant in Bur Dubai, a supper club in JVC, an Italian bakery for a cake, or the menu from a food truck someone ate at last month. If that is the search, book the venue. You want their room, their address and their service, and no caterer replaces that.

Catering runs the other way. The kitchen travels to the address you give us, and the room and the guest list stay yours: a villa in Dubai Hills, an office in Business Bay, a terrace at Dubai Creek Harbour, a family home in Bur Dubai, a hall in Festival City, a hotel function room you have already taken, a beach house or a yacht. Same cuisine, cooked on site, no table booked at somebody else's restaurant and no closing time. Drop-off and delivery work the same way when you want the food without the staffing.

On budget: if you searched for cheap Italian catering in Dubai, the format sets the floor, not the cuisine. Drop-off trays and a plain buffet cost far less per head than plated service with a chef and waiters, and the same pasta comes out of the same pot either way. Volume formats start at 10 guests, a full buffet at 20, and the site-wide minimum order value is AED 900. Tell us the ceiling you are working to and we build the menu down to it instead of sending a quote you have to argue with.

From AED 90 per person dropped off, AED 120 for a staffed buffet and AED 150 with a live pasta or pizza station. A chef cooking and plating on site is AED 700 to 950 per person. Minimums are 10 guests on volume formats, 20 on a buffet and AED 900 on order value, with 5% VAT added.
What is included in italian catering services dubai?

Everything from menu planning to delivery is included: the chef, service staff, plating, all equipment and full setup and cleanup. One team covers the whole event, so you are not coordinating separate vendors.
Can I hire a private italian chef dubai for a small dinner?

Yes. A private italian chef dubai suits intimate dinners just as well as large events — the chef plans the menu, cooks in your kitchen and clears up, with pricing quoted per head at AED 700 to 950 and no minimum headcount.
Do you offer italian catering packages dubai?
We do. Clear italian catering packages let you compare formats — buffet, plated or live stations — and budgets before you commit, and every package is quoted itemised for your exact guest count.
Is affordable italian catering dubai possible without dropping quality?

Affordable italian catering dubai is genuinely possible at the entry tier. Buffet and drop-off formats bring the per-head cost down while a vetted chef still prepares the food fresh, not reheated in trays.
Can you cater corporate italian catering dubai events?

Yes. Corporate italian catering dubai covers boardroom lunches, conference buffets and gala dinners, scheduled around your working day and invoiced for business. Tell us the headcount and we scale the menu and staffing to match.
How do I book?
Share your date, guest count and venue. We match a vetted chef and send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day and promptly for a first response during our published business hours.
Do you do italian catering delivery, or only a chef on site?

Both. Delivered Italian catering starts at AED 90 per person with a 10-guest minimum, and arrives ready to serve. A chef cooking on site is AED 700 to 950 per person. Fresh pasta, risotto and wood-fired pizza are worth the on-site option, since each has a short window before it changes; a drop-off menu is built from dishes that hold.
For italian catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .
